_doc: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the cluster's layer/group topology. The orchestrator, world-stamps.py (json.load), provision.sh + stream-region-to-box.sh (jq) all DERIVE from this — never re-encode a group's layers/arrows/seed/binary by hand (that is the fix-one-miss-the-rest drift this file removes). Its SIBLING SSOT is scripts/output-versions.json, the painted-byte era per layer: a layer whose worker binary changes here needs its era bumped there in the SAME commit, which scripts/test-layer-spec.mjs enforces. A layer's arrows is the orchestration read set currently consumed for data-version invalidation, region transport and stage inclusion; this documentation-only change neither changes nor certifies that set's composition. dependency_arrows documents the subset of those declared arrows whose presence alone must not create a task; every dependency arrow is also in arrows. This field is classification metadata only: current readers intentionally continue to consume arrows unchanged, and the planner still over-approximates buildability from arrows until the pending dual-reviewed read-set/buildability split lands. Derived, NOT stored: a group's stage-excludes = every layer arrow NOT in its own layers; the tile-layer set = the union of all groups' layers. NOT covered here: layer-codever.py's per-layer engine-source-file partition (DEFAULT_EXCL) — that is code-versioning, not topology, and stays its own authority. Placeholders {OUTPUT} {SEED} {H3R4} {PREP} {ZOOM} in worker_types.flags are substituted at launch. relevant-source-surface takes its prepared root from the environment variable NOISE_GPU_PREPARED and derives its h3r4 tree from it, so its flags carry none of {PREP} {H3R4} {SEED}; seed_arrow exists exactly for the groups whose flags still carry {SEED}.

surface._doc: The five ground layers one relevant-source-surface process paints from ONE preparation of a cell: it loads the cell's ring once, builds each 4x4 batch's terrain halo once, and paints whatever subset the cell line's layers= names. GPU-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION — there is deliberately no CPU worker type here, and a planner reads the absence of one as 'this group needs a card'. build-heatmap-surface stays in the tree as the etalon producer for parity work; it is a DIFFERENT renderer and must never paint production tiles for these layers.

gpu-surface._doc: Worker type name (the orchestrator's profile key), not a binary: it runs relevant-source-surface. The benchmark painter binary also called gpu-surface is a different renderer and is not deployed.
